G1 durability [G1.durability] 300 events, a broker killed mid-run, then the API and the consumer SIGKILLed: every 202 is stored after restart
S3-F8 late and out-of-order events (API -> Kafka -> sink) [G5.reorder-late] dataset D shuffled, 10% 1 min / 1 h / 24 h late, some sent seconds later: the table equals D exactly

S3-F8 late and out-of-order events (API -> Kafka -> sink) [G5.retry-late] a record waits on a retry tier while NEWER events of the tenant are stored first: both stored, occurred_at correct, received_at the original
S3-F8 late and out-of-order events (API -> Kafka -> sink) [G5.replay-late] DLQ replay of an old event: stored with its ORIGINAL received_at (it does not look new)

S3-F8 late and out-of-order events (API -> Kafka -> sink) [G5.skew] occurred_at 1 year + 1 day old -> 422 occurred_at_too_old, 10 min ahead -> 422 occurred_at_in_future, no zone -> 400; nothing produced
S3-F8 late and out-of-order events (API -> Kafka -> sink) the sink measures lateness of what it stores (ep_sink_lateness_seconds)
S3-F8 property: order and lateness do not change what is stored [G5.property] BatchWriter, 1000 runs: stored set == first-wins reference; counts, min/max(occurred_at), duplicates and conflicts match
S3-F8 property through the pipeline (API -> Kafka -> sink) [G5.property-pipeline] 20 runs: shuffled, late (0 s .. 24 h), resends mixed in, concurrent sends: stored == sent, received_at = server time
G4 ordering [G4.per-key-order] two tenants interleaved, sequence numbers in the payload, read from the log: per key, one partition and offsets in sequence order
S3-F4 outbox relay with Kafka down [G7.kafka-down] 30 s outage while changes keep coming: backlog and oldest age grow, nothing lost, all published in order afterwards
S3-F4 admin-api: config change + outbox row in one transaction [G7.commit-published] PUT config: version + 1, exactly 1 outbox row, the relay publishes it, it decodes with the registered schema

S3-F4 admin-api: config change + outbox row in one transaction [G7.no-enqueue-on-reject] optimistic concurrency and validation: 412 stale If-Match, 404 unknown tenant, 400 bad body, 401 without the admin key; none of them enqueues

S3-F4 admin-api: config change + outbox row in one transaction [G7.rollback-error] rolled back (injected error after the outbox insert, before COMMIT): no config change, no outbox row, nothing published

S3-F4 admin-api: config change + outbox row in one transaction [G7.rollback-crash] crash at admin:after-update-before-commit: the process dies with the transaction open, nothing commits, nothing is published
S3-F4 outbox-relay: at least once, crash points [G7.relay-before-publish] crash at relay:before-publish: published after the restart, 0 lost, 0 duplicates sent
S3-F4 outbox-relay: at least once, crash points [G7.relay-after-publish] crash at relay:after-publish-before-mark: the batch is published twice, attempts = 2, the consumer applies each change once
S3-F4 outbox-relay: at least once, crash points [G7.relay-after-mark] crash at relay:after-mark-before-commit: the mark rolls back with the connection, the batch is republished
S3-F4 two relays [G7.single-leader] single-leader mode, 1000 ordered changes of one tenant: version order on the topic; the standby takes over when the leader is killed
S3-F4 two relays [G7.multi-mode] RELAY_MODE=multi, 1000 changes: order violations measured (not asserted), the consumer still ends on the latest version
S3-F4 two relays [G7.retention] graceful stop releases the lock at once and the backlog gauge reads 0 when drained; retention deletes old published rows
S3-F4 publish latency (commit -> published), LISTEN vs polling only [G7.latency] listen: 100 changes 20 ms apart, latency from the outbox row itself
S3-F4 publish latency (commit -> published), LISTEN vs polling only [G7.latency] poll_200ms: 100 changes 20 ms apart, latency from the outbox row itself
S3-F2 replay safety (real process, real log) [G3.triple-replay] the same log consumed 3 times: storage unchanged, duplicates = 2N
S3-F2 replay safety (real process, real log) [G3.range-replay] replaying from the middle of every partition: storage unchanged, duplicates = replayed records
S3-F5 retry tiers and DLQ (real process) [G6.permanent] an unparseable record: one DLQ record + one dlq_meta row with full metadata, no retry traffic
S3-F5 retry tiers and DLQ (real process) [G6.transient-recovers] a row failing with 40001 on the main path is stored from tier 1 after its delay; the records behind it do not wait
S3-F5 retry tiers and DLQ (real process) [G6.never-recovers] a row that keeps failing: tiers 1, 2, 3, then the DLQ with attempts 3, origin = the source record
S3-F5 retry tiers and DLQ (real process) [G6.outage] Postgres unreachable for 15 s: the partition pauses; ZERO retry or DLQ records; everything stored after
S3-F5 retry tiers and DLQ (real process) [G6.rate-limit] more retriable rows than RETRY_MAX_RATE_PER_S: the partition is paused instead of flooding the tiers
S3-F5 retry tiers and DLQ (real process) [G6.poison-in-batch] 1 poison record among 500: 499 stored, 1 dead letter, no retry traffic for the good rows
